name: AI-authorship PR detectors (pr-slop-filter, deslop-kitten, TuringMerge, …)
description: GitHub Actions that try to detect AI-generated PRs from textual and diff 'tells' and block or label them. A GitHub repository search found several such projects, each with fewer than 5 stars.
weaknesses: Target AI authorship, while several major projects explicitly allow AI-assisted work
False positives on legitimate AI-assisted contributions (inference)
Low adoption

name: Microsoft API Extractor
description: A TypeScript tool that snapshots a library's public API (.d.ts) so changes can be reviewed, among several other jobs (doc generation, .d.ts rollups).
weaknesses: Heavy setup aimed at larger teams (inference)
Type surface only

name: cargo-semver-checks (Rust)
description: Rust's established semver linter with a GitHub Action. It checks a crate's public API before publishing. About 1,700 GitHub stars at retrieval.
weaknesses: Rust only
Documents violations it can't catch

name: Auto-closing all external pull requests
description: tldraw closes PRs from external contributors by default and selectively reopens the ones under consideration.
weaknesses: Gives up outside contributions entirely; the maintainer calls it temporary and regrettable

name: Dependabot cooldown
description: Delays Dependabot update PRs for newly published versions. GA since July 2025.
strengths: Free on GitHub; adopted mainly for security
weaknesses: Only affects automated update PRs, not manual installs (inference)

name: Fossier
description: GitHub Action that scores unknown PR authors on 13 account and content signals (account age, follower ratio, PR description quality…) and auto-allows, flags or closes PRs.
weaknesses: Account-reputation signals penalise genuine newcomers (inference)
Heuristics are gameable (inference)
Small adoption (~41 stars at retrieval)

name: GitHub pull-request access settings & interaction limits
description: Native repository controls: disable pull requests, restrict them to collaborators, or apply interaction limits (existing users, prior contributors, collaborators).
weaknesses: Coarse: restricting to collaborators or prior contributors also shuts out legitimate newcomers (inference)
No assessment of contribution quality

name: npm staged publishing + token-free publishing settings
description: Opt-in npm features: releases are staged and must be approved by a maintainer with 2FA; a package setting can forbid token publishing; trusted publishers can be limited to staging.
strengths: Free and built into the registry
weaknesses: Opt-in: protects only maintainers who enable it
A human approving a release still has to notice what changed (inference)
Launched May 2026; adoption unknown

name: pnpm minimumReleaseAge
description: pnpm setting that refuses to install versions younger than a configured age.
weaknesses: pnpm users only (npm and bun requested it separately)

name: PyPI warning when an API token uploads to a trusted-publishing project
description: An email to maintainers when a long-lived token is used for a project configured for trusted publishing.
strengths: Catches the stolen-token pattern on projects that migrated
weaknesses: Only for projects with trusted publishing configured
No general notice of every new release (none among PyPI's email templates)

name: Registry trusted publishing (OIDC) on npm and PyPI
description: Publish from CI using short-lived OIDC identity instead of long-lived tokens.
weaknesses: npm can't use it for a package's first version

name: Commercial supply-chain scanners (e.g. Socket, StepSecurity)
description: Vendors that analyse new package releases and publish incident write-ups. Named in the captured issues; their products were not examined in this run.
strengths: Already detect and report incidents quickly (inference from their write-ups being cited)
weaknesses: Not examined in this run

name: Maintainer triage conventions (autoclose labels, template-compliance rules)
description: Lightweight project workflows that cut per-PR triage effort: scikit-learn's proposed autoclose label, and nixpkgs' proposal to close PRs that remove the AI-disclosure checkboxes.
strengths: Cheap, transparent, keeps a human in the loop
weaknesses: A human still has to look at each PR to apply the label
Template rules are easy to game (inference)

name: New TypeScript semver checkers (Clerk break-check, ts-semver-checks, semver-check)
description: Several 2026 projects that diff the exported TypeScript surface between versions and fail CI on an insufficient version bump. Clerk's is company-backed and uses API Extractor plus an AI review.
weaknesses: Very new; little adoption (0–3 stars at retrieval)
Type surface only: blind to engines, exports and other metadata breaks

name: Vouch (mitchellh/vouch)
description: Explicit trust lists: trusted people vouch for contributors, bad actors can be denounced. GitHub Actions integration. Used by Ghostty.
weaknesses: Requires a social path to get vouched (cold start for newcomers, inference)
Public denouncement lists carry governance and abuse risks (inference)
Self-described as experimental

name: Written AI contribution policies + canned responses
description: Projects publish AI policies (LLVM, Linux, QEMU, curl, Ghostty, scikit-learn, Zulip, Godot) and close violating PRs with a standard response. LLVM provides a paste-able reply.
strengths: Sets norms and gives maintainers a cheap way to close
weaknesses: Enforcement still requires a human to read each submission
Relies on contributors reading the policy
